who: A retired teacher who chairs the allotment association and looks after two grandchildren on Wednesdays.

moments.plot: The annual meeting is on Thursday, and the hall wants its key back.

tasks.title: Bring Ruth the spare key
tasks.notes: The hall, not the shed. The shed key has the green tag.

tasks.title: Print the agenda, large
tasks.notes: Thirty copies. Gerald brings his own glasses but never finds them.

tasks.title: Put the waiting list in order
Ask Gerald if his van is free for chairs
New wellies for the small one

file.title: Who takes the minutes this year?
file.notes: Ruth did the last four and has said so.

dated.title: Set out the chairs
dated.notes: Six rows of five. Leave the side door free for the pushchairs.

repeating.title: Check the frost fleece
repeating.notes: Stones on the corners. The wind found it last week.

attachments.notes: Two kinds without nuts. Ruth has the big tins. Last year’s list is attached, and it was not enough.

tasks.title: Give the hall its key back

agent.title: Turn last year’s notes into minutes
agent.notes: Nine handwritten pages, typed up by Ruth. The meeting has to agree them.
agent.question: How long should the minutes be?
bodies: Present: 27 members. Rents stay the same. The path gets new gravel. The hedge question moves to the next meeting.
1. Welcome, 27 members present. 2. Rents stay the same, 21 for and 6 against. 3. New gravel for the path before April. 4. The hedge, discussed and moved to the next meeting.
agent.otherBody: Present: 27 members. Rents, the path and the hedge were discussed. Your direction: {answer}
agent.acceptance: The minutes are ready for the meeting to agree.

discuss.title: Reply about the hedge
discuss.notes: The couple from plot 14 want it lower. Gerald planted it.
discuss.question: What would you like to happen?
bodies: Thank you for your note about the hedge. I have put it on the agenda for the meeting, so everyone can hear it and vote.
Thank you for your note about the hedge. I would like the three of us to look at it with Gerald first. He planted it and may have an idea.
discuss.otherBody: Thank you for your note about the hedge. Here is what I suggest: {answer}

review.title: Turn last year’s notes into minutes
review.note: One page. I could not read one name on page six.

review.title: Sort the waiting list by date
review.note: Thirty-three names. Two people are on it twice.

faded: Write to the cousin in Leeds
